pull.title: test: fix race in Tor control reconnect check
pull.body:
`feature_torcontrol.py` can fail if the node reconnects before the test thread starts checking the backoff. This caused an intermittent CI failure on NetBSD even though the node observed the expected delay.

Record when the mock Tor server accepts the new connection and compare that timestamp with the time just before triggering the disconnect. This preserves both checks: at least half a second must have elapsed, and the node must send `PROTOCOLINFO 1` on reconnect.

On Linux, the 1.5-second delay from the issue reproduced the original failure. The updated test passed both with and without that delay.

Fixes #36934.

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

tACK ba7734b

Reproduced #36934. On master, `ensure_for` check fails immediately, and on this branch it passes. 

Also checked the new assertion still fails when the backoff is genuinely missing. Set `RECONNECT_TIMEOUT_START` to 0.0 and rebuilding:
```
test_oversized_line: AssertionError: 0.013399518000369426 < 0.5
test_overmany_lines: AssertionError: 0.013552839998737909 < 0.5 (run on its own)
```
Clearly, almost all of the 0.5s threshold has to come from the node's actual wait.

Ran `feature_torcontrol.py` 5 times on this branch with backoff restored, all passing.

Concept ACK

EDIT: and Approach ACK

comments.body:
I think this comment could be a bit clearer:

```suggestion
            # No reconnect before the initial reconnect timeout of 1s has passed.
            # Measured from before the disconnect was triggered, so a slow test
            # can only increase the elapsed time.
```
